name: Data Room
description: Prepare, share and track data rooms for financing, licensing, partnering and M&A, with diligence Q&A built in. A standard 9-section biotech index weighted by purpose, a readiness checklist with owners and due dates, documents from the platform document store (one set reused across rooms, versions kept in place), levels (Non-confidential, Confidential and custom) with a click-through or signed-CDA entry step, one private link per person with no recipient accounts, emails from TrialAgents in one confirmed send, per-person and per-document engagement, structured Q&A with approval and private or published answers, and a disclosure record. Notify all or chosen parties about new documents in one confirmed send, an access-ending reminder per room, instant emails for party questions, and a weekly room summary. Claude and ChatGPT can run every action through app commands and customize forms, fields and templates. Writes the dataroom.v1 outputs that Fundraise and Partnerships read.
whenToUse: A small biotech prepares or runs a data room for a round, licensing, partnering or M&A: index, readiness, sharing with investors or partners, levels, CDA, tracking who viewed what, diligence Q&A.
whenNotToUse: General file storage, board portals, contract drafting or e-signature (use Contracts for the register), investor update emails (Investor Updates), cap-table management, watermarking, redaction or eCTD viewing.

heading.description: App heading shown above every screen.

tableMap.description: JSON object keyed by stable role key: core data contract v1 roles organizations (required) and people, programs, agreements (optional; agreements binds the core fields only); app roles dataroom.settings, dataroom.templates, dataroom.rooms, dataroom.levels, dataroom.sections, dataroom.items, dataroom.questions and the published outputs dataroom.access_grants and dataroom.engagement (contract dataroom.v1; this app is their writer). Each value is {typeId:<authorized table UUID>, fields:{<logical key>:<real field key>}, writableFields:[<logical keys>]}. Real keys are lowercase snake_case. The installer writes it; never invent table IDs.

pageSize.description: Rows per page in registers (10 to 50).

layoutProfile.description: Stringified native layout profile (heading, tabs, cols, visible) written by the layout gear review. Do not edit by hand.

readOnly.description: Disable every write control in this copy.

demoLabel.description: Label the data as fictional (offline preview only).

asOfOverride.description: Pinned as-of date YYYY-MM-DD for previews and tests. Leave empty in real apps: the app uses today's date.

instructions:
Data Room 1.1.0 is a custom frontend-js app (Vivid kit, theme forest) for data rooms in financing, licensing, partnering and M&A, with diligence Q&A (it also covers the former Diligence Q&A scope). Read read_app_template_guidance (usage, authoring and contracts, every nextOffset; guidance 1.3.32 or later, especially "External exchange from apps", "Exchange rooms" and "Platform documents inside apps") before preparing it. Pin life.data-room 1.1.0 with its digest. Do not add login, accounts, a portal, email code, file storage or viewers: rooms are the platform exchange in room mode.
INSTALL. Check list_archived_items (kind apps, templateId life.data-room) and offer to restore an archived app first. Use installs the app with empty tables. The Use existing data? dialog connects existing organizations, people, programs or agreements tables by default (core.v1; reuse, never copy); everything else gets new dataroom.* tables. Data Room writes the outputs dataroom.access_grants and dataroom.engagement (dataroom.v1); another app that already writes them keeps writing unless the owner takes over after archiving it. Assistants may propose choices with prepare_data_access and never confirm them. No records are seeded; the financing, licensing, partnering and M&A index templates are built in.
SET-UP. New room (purpose, programs, Fundraise round and Partnerships opportunity references, index template, CDA option, welcome note, contact person) → set up levels and sections (one review: Non-confidential and Confidential; the Confidential entry step follows the CDA option) → add the checklist items from the template (one review) → attach platform documents to items with level and view-only → make the room live. Readiness = ready ÷ (required − not applicable), per room and per section.
EXCHANGE (guidance 1.3.25 rooms). One room group per room: exchange.createGroup({kind:"room",appRef:"room:<room id>",levels,slots,documents:[{versionId,title,section,order,level,viewOnly,toSign}],tracking:{accessTypeId,engagementTypeId},notifyEngagement,notifyAccessEnding,quietDays,emailDefaults}). Level keys are "l"+the level record ID without dashes; entry none / click_through (Settings text) / signed_document (signed_cda, with its own slot signed_<level key>). One exchange per person bound to its dataroom.access_grants record (exchange.invite with recordId, and the levels for everyone in that invitation). Invitations: exchange.prepareEmail access_granted, shown exactly as returned, then exchange.sendEmail; nothing is sent without that confirmation. Index changes: exchange.shareDocuments({add,update,remove}); new versions: exchange.replaceDocument (same place, Updated for parties). Levels: exchange.setLevels (with entered + enteredNote for a CDA in place elsewhere or on file in Contracts) and exchange.defineLevels for custom levels. Signed CDA: exchange.acceptFile on the level slot opens only that level and emails the person. Q&A: questions arrive in exchange.listQuestions, are logged as dataroom.questions, answered with exchange.answer (private) or exchange.publishAnswer (scope room or level, asker anonymised). Notify parties (no automatic digest): the person picks documents and all or chosen parties; exchange.prepareEmail documents_updated with exchangeIds and versionIds (each person is told only about chosen documents they can open), shown exactly as returned, then exchange.sendEmail. Access-ending reminder per room: rooms.access_ending_reminder, and exchange.setRoomNotices({groupId,expectedVersion,notifyAccessEnding}) for a live room. Revoke and extend: exchange.revoke / exchange.extend. Archiving a live room: exchange.archiveGroup. Granting, levels, publishing, answers, acceptance, revocation and sends are confirmed by a person; assistants draft only.
TRACKED DATA. TrialAgents keeps dataroom.access_grants status (invited / active / revoked / expired), last_seen_on and source (tracked), and one dataroom.engagement row per person and document (views, seconds, downloads, first and last viewed, as_of). These fields are read-only to people, assistants and this app. Archiving a room's app stops links and updates.
AI. Assistants read rooms and Q&A records the user can read and documents only where the document's AI setting allows; they never see links. They draft indexes, readiness plans, invitation and notification texts (prepare_exchange_email), answers with document references and engagement summaries. They never send, grant, change levels, publish, accept or revoke, and never advise on what is legally safe to disclose.
COMMANDS (guidance 1.3.31+). list_app_commands lists 32 commands; run_app_command runs the saved app's own code with your access. Read commands return the app's own results (rooms.read, waiting.read, index.read, readiness.read, parties.read, activity.read, changes.read, brief.read, questions.read, notify.read, settings.read, schema.describe): report them, never recompute readiness, hot or quiet parties or briefs yourself. Propose commands go through the same handler as the clicks and return the exact review (room.create, room.setup_structure, room.setup_items, room.status, record.save for any form, record.archive, item.attach, item.use_version, party.add, party.levels before a link exists, questions.log, question.save save/approve/decline, settings.save, email_text.save/reset, template.copy/save, custom_field.save/remove); confirm with confirm_workspace_change only after the user agrees. layout.save changes screens, columns and forms (room_form, item_form, question_form: order, hide optional fields, labels, defaults). Commands never share, send, grant, change a live room, accept, revoke, answer or publish: those are a person's clicks; prepare emails with prepare_exchange_email and room changes with prepare_workspace_change for the person to confirm. CUSTOMIZE. Custom fields on rooms, index items, parties and questions: custom_field.save registers it in settings.custom_fields and returns the schema change still needed (prepare_change update_type on that table, then an app revision that changes only the binding). The app then shows the field in its form, details and command results. Changing the app's code needs full access (owner, or a member with nothing hidden); keep changes in layout, settings and records where possible. NOTIFICATIONS AND AUTOMATION. The room owner and members with the external-send right get an email at once for each party question, note, requested upload and first open (platform). One install recommendation, on by default: the weekly room summary email to the owner, Mondays 08:00 Europe/Berlin, written by the app helper room_summary from the app's records. There is no automatic digest to parties and no answer-drafting automation: users ask the assistant in chat.

quickStart: Read the current usage, authoring and contracts guidance and this documentation; pin life.data-room 1.0.0 and its digest with one requestKey.
Check for an archived Data Room app and offer to restore it. Otherwise Use installs it; keep the defaults that connect existing organizations, people, programs and agreements tables.
Settings: adjust default access length, quiet days, Q&A approval, the click-through text and the email texts per type and purpose.
Rooms: create a room, set up levels and sections, then add the checklist items from the template.
Index: attach documents to items, choose the level and view-only, watch readiness; preview the room as a party.
Make the room live, add parties, give access and confirm one invitation send. Follow engagement on Activity and answer questions on Q&A.
documentation.dataContract: Stable role keys; every field scalar (multiple false), lowercase snake_case, relationships by record ID in text fields. Core data contract v1: organizations (name*, org_type, country, website, archived), people (optional: name*, organization_id, title, email, archived), programs (optional), agreements (optional; core fields only; CDAs filed with agreement_type cda_nda). App tables, contract dataroom.v1: dataroom.settings (one row: default_access_days 180, blank = until revoked; view_only_default false; quiet_days 10; qa_approval_required true; entry_text; sender_display organization/first_name; email_texts JSON {<email type>:{<purpose>|all:{subject,body}}}; custom_fields JSON [{role rooms/items/grants/questions,key,label,kind text/longtext/number/date/select/boolean,options}]), dataroom.templates (name*, purpose*, content JSON {sections:[{number,name,items:[{title,required,level,weight}]}]}, archived), dataroom.rooms (name*, purpose* financing/licensing/partnering/m_and_a/other, status* preparing/live/closed, program_ids, round_id, opportunity_ref, template_id, cda_option* send_pdf/contracts/in_place/none, welcome_note, contact_person_id, access_ending_reminder (default on), exchange_group_id, owner, archived), dataroom.levels (room_id*, name*, kind* non_confidential/confidential/custom, order*, entry* none/click_through/signed_cda), dataroom.sections (room_id*, number*, name*, parent_id, order*), dataroom.items (room_id*, section_id*, title*, required, status* missing/in_progress/ready/not_applicable, owner, due, document_id, version_id, level_id*, view_only, updated_on, notes), dataroom.questions (room_id*, grant_id, organization_id, person_id, asked_on*, category, section_id, item_id, question*, status* new/assigned/drafting/in_review/answered/published/declined, assignee, due, answer, approved_by, answered_on, visibility private/room/level, level_id, reused_from, document_ids, message_id). Published outputs (writer life.data-room, dataroom.v1, read by Fundraise, Partnerships and custom apps): dataroom.access_grants (room_id, room_name, room_purpose financing/licensing/partnering/m_and_a/other, organization_id, person_id, granted_on, expires_on, status, agreement_accepted_on, source manual/tracked; app fields level_ids, recipient_email*, exchange_id, cda_status not_needed/sent/signed/in_place_elsewhere, cda_agreement_id, last_seen_on) and dataroom.engagement (grant_id, organization_id, person_id, document_ref, document_title, first_viewed_on, last_viewed_on, view_count, seconds_viewed, downloads, source manual/docsend/sharevault/tracked, as_of; app field section_id). Data Room writes only source tracked; status, last_seen_on and every engagement row are platform-kept and read-only. agreement_accepted_on is set by the app when a CDA is accepted or recorded as in place.
documentation.interactionContract: Seven screens with stable IDs for the native layout gear: overview, rooms, index, parties, activity, qa, settings; column groups parties and questions; form groups room_form, item_form and question_form (order, hide optional fields, labels, defaults). A room picker selects the room on every room screen; party, document and question details open in the side panel. Overview: rooms with purpose, status, readiness and invited/active people; activity (opens this week, new viewers, hot and quiet parties); waiting on us (new and overdue questions, signed CDAs to accept, items due); recent changes and emails sent. Rooms: new room, set-up steps, levels with entry steps and custom levels, branding (title, welcome note, contact), status, Notify parties (chosen documents to all or chosen parties, one confirmed send) and the access-ending reminder switch. Index: numbered sections and items with readiness per section, attach documents (platform upload or an existing document), level and view-only, newer versions offered in place, publish index changes to the room, preview as a party at a level. Parties: parties with levels, CDA, status, granted, ends and last seen; add party, give access and invite in one confirmed send with personalisation; levels with CDA options; accept a signed CDA; revoke; extend; disclosure record. Activity: engagement grid by party and section, per-document opens with versions, time and downloads, quiet and hot parties, what changed since each party's last visit and a call brief to copy. Q&A: new questions from the room, the log with assign/draft/approve/answer privately/publish/decline, approved answers and repeated-question suggestions. Settings: index templates (copy and edit), email texts per type and purpose, defaults, custom fields, access, notifications and automation. Every action is also an app command (list_app_commands).
documentation.lifecycle: A new preview shows empty or fictional data, never writes and never contacts anyone; exchange and document capabilities need the saved app. Saved apps re-read their tables, the room groups and configuration on every render. Record writes are records.propose batches (at most 50 per review) confirmed in the TrialAgents review; a stale version is rejected with the draft kept. Exchange writes are one per click: preparation nobody outside has seen (creating the room, links, documents) is applied on the person's click; sends, level changes, answers, publications, acceptances, reminder switches and revocations are reviewed and carry the app's record changes in the same transaction. Layout changes are reviewed presentation-only edits. Archive first: archiving a room record is a reviewed change; archiving the app stops every link and tracked update; restoring re-enables only unexpired grants. Fundraise keeps working with "data unavailable" while the app is archived.
limitations: Hosted rooms only: no external-room mode, watermarking, screenshot blocking, page-by-page analytics, redaction, eCTD viewer, custom domains or recipient accounts. View-only hides the download but cannot stop screenshots.
The inline viewer shows PDF and images; other files download (unless view-only). Engagement is approximate visible time from viewer heartbeats.

Fundraise and Partnerships publish no round or opportunity tables as roles, so parties are picked from shared organizations and people and the round and opportunity are kept as references. Fundraise and Partnerships read this app's dataroom.v1 outputs.

E-signature is out: a signed CDA is uploaded back and accepted by a workspace owner. "Use Contracts" files the accepted CDA as a core agreements record (cda_nda) for Contracts; link it to the party from Levels.
A review holds at most 50 record changes: set-up runs as two reviews (levels and sections, then the checklist items), and templates hold at most 50 items.
Not legal advice on what to disclose.
Custom fields are shown in forms, details and command results, not as table columns or filters, and are never used in readiness or engagement.
Commands prepare records only; anything that shares, sends or changes a live room is a person's click in the app.

examples.prompt: Set up a data room for our Series B and get it ready for investors next week.
examples.expectedBehavior: Proposes one dataroom.rooms record (purpose financing, template builtin:financing, CDA option as discussed) and explains the two set-up reviews and the readiness gaps; drafts a readiness plan with owners and dates. Sends nothing.

examples.prompt: Invite Alder Peak and Birchway to the Series B room; personalise Ana's email to mention our call.
examples.expectedBehavior: Proposes the access_grants rows if missing. After the user gives access in the app, prepares the access_granted batch with prepare_exchange_email with an override for Ana, and tells the user to review and confirm the send in the app. Never sends or confirms.

examples.prompt: What has Cedarline looked at since our last call, and which investors are hot in the Series B room?
examples.expectedBehavior: Runs brief.read for Cedarline's grant and parties.read for the room, and reports the app's own results (opens, changes since their last visit, open questions, hot and quiet flags). Computes nothing itself and never sees links.

examples.prompt: Draft answers for the new questions in the licensing room.
examples.expectedBehavior: Runs questions.read, logs new room questions with questions.log, reads only AI-readable documents, and saves drafts with question.save (step save) for review, reusing approved answers for repeated questions. Never approves on the user's behalf, answers or publishes.

examples.prompt: Add a 'Deal code' field to rooms, and on the item form hide Owner and rename Due to Target date.
examples.expectedBehavior: Runs custom_field.save (rooms, deal_code, text) and prepares the schema change and binding-only app revision it returns; then layout.save with hide ['item_form:owner'] and labels {'item_form:due':'Target date'}. Each is one review; the app code is unchanged.

tasks.whenUseful: One install recommendation, selected by default and optional: a weekly room summary email to the owner (Mondays 08:00 Europe/Berlin) with new viewers, active and quiet parties, open and overdue questions and checklist items due, written by the app helper room_summary. The app works fully without it. Party notifications are not automated: a person uses Notify parties. Access-ending reminders are a per-room switch. Questions and notes from parties are emailed to the owner at once by the platform.
tasks.readRequirements: dataroom.rooms, dataroom.access_grants, dataroom.engagement, dataroom.questions, dataroom.items, dataroom.settings, organizations and people records the owner can read (helper room_summary, records.read only).
tasks.outputContract: One email to the owner per week while a room is live; nothing when no room is live (nonEmpty false). No record writes.
tasks.promptExample: Without an automation, ask the assistant: "Summarise this week in the Series B room" (it runs activity.read, waiting.read and questions.read).
